title: Testing
description: Unit-test ideas expressed as small stdout-checked programs (adapted for this platform).
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Testing

Real code uses xUnit/NUnit; stdout exercises here mirror assertions as printable outcomes.

exercises.title: Basic test (stdout)
exercises.description: Implement `Sum` and print `Sum(2, 3)` (same intent as the C# `#[test]` exercise).
exercises.starter_code:
static int Sum(int a, int b) => 0;
Console.WriteLine(Sum(2, 3));
exercises.solution:
static int Sum(int a, int b) => a + b;
Console.WriteLine(Sum(2, 3));

exercises.title: Table cases (stdout)
exercises.description: Print three integers on one line: `Multiply(2,3)`, `Multiply(0,5)`, `Multiply(-1,4)`.
exercises.starter_code:
static int Multiply(int a, int b) => 0;
// Console.WriteLine($"{Multiply(2,3)} {Multiply(0,5)} {Multiply(-1,4)}");
exercises.solution:
static int Multiply(int a, int b) => a * b;
Console.WriteLine($"{Multiply(2, 3)} {Multiply(0, 5)} {Multiply(-1, 4)}");

exercises.title: Divide and error (stdout)
exercises.description: Print `ok` if `Divide(10,2)` is 5 and `Divide(10,0)` is null (use `int?`).
exercises.starter_code:
static int? Divide(int a, int b) => default;
// if (...) Console.Write("ok");
exercises.solution:
static int? Divide(int a, int b) => b == 0 ? null : a / b;
if (Divide(10, 2) == 5 && Divide(10, 0) is null) Console.Write("ok");

exercises.title: Error message check (stdout)
exercises.description: If `Validate(-5)` returns an error message containing `negative`, print `yes`; else print `no`.
exercises.solution:
static string Validate(int age) => age < 0 ? "age cannot be negative" : "ok";
Console.Write(Validate(-5).Contains("negative") ? "yes" : "no");

exercises.title: Hot path loop (stdout)
exercises.description: After calling `Sum(2,3)` ten thousand times in a loop, print `done`.
hints: Keep `Sum` trivial; the loop is the point.
